ratings.comment: Prof. Schulte is amazing! She is super passionate about the subject which makes listening to lectures really easy and entertaining. Attendance is not mandatory and the homework is relatively light, there are 3 main projects but they are more time consuming than difficult, and 3 exams which are open note/book including the final and are all online!

She clearly cares about anthro and her lectures were interesting, but you don't have to attend lecture to do well in this course. Overall, this course was very easy, the three fieldwork projects were somewhat time consuming.

This is honestly an easy class. I only attended lectures for the first 2 weeks, and still got a pretty good grade. All you really have to do is read the assigned chapters, participate in weekly discussions, do the homework, and complete the fieldwork projects. The reason I rated it a 4 is because almost all the homework is busywork and tedious.
She's a pretty good professor, but the class is mainly busy work and is pretty tedious.

Professor Schulte is super knowledgable and the lectures are very interesting. She makes an effort to remember names (and actually does) when theres 350+ people in the lecture and she definitely cares about the subject. The class is pretty easy to do well in. Would recommend!

Lecture attendance was not required and you didn't need to be there to understand what would be on the online exams. There is a textbook and weekly quizzes that were pretty simple. There were three projects and a few other assignments which were are very doable as well.

Very easy class, one of the three projects is tricky because it requires you to find and interview an immigrant(international students DON'T count), lectures are optional and I would recommend just skipping.

She is a great teacher and I really liked the topics that we talked about. The fieldwork projects are also easy, though there is one about an interview with an immigrant that was hard, but other than that everything else is very easy. The tests are also online and open-note, so they are very easy if you take notes on the book and lecture.

Anthro 104 is such an easy but interesting class. Lectures are not mandatory and few students attend. She speaks quite quickly and does not share slides, but lectures tended to be more application of the material, so I did not need to take notes during lecture. There are 3 open, non-proctored exams and 3 projects that were all easy.

I think that Dr. Schulte is a great professor, however the class itself requires a lot of reading. It takes a lot of time to complete the chapter readings each week, but doing so will set you up very well for lecture discussions.

This class was very easy, and professor was very passionate about what she was teaching. Lectures were not necessary to attend, but you should/have to go to discussion, which most of the time can be pretty engaging and entertaining. There are 3 online tests and 3 projects, but other than that, there's really nothing to worry about.

This class was really easy and Prof Schulte was very passionate in her lectures! She did talk fairly fast, making it hard to take notes and didn't share her slides, but reading the textbook will help fill in the gaps. Projects are solo and were really easy/borderline busywork. Your TA will be the biggest influence on your experience, though.

I like her a lot!! Sometimes rushes through lecture slides quite fast, and doesn't post the slides. It can be easy to lose attention for a second, and miss what she said on a previous slide. But, if you do the readings youll be fine!! Grading really depends on your TA, but for me grading has been pretty generous.

Didn't often go to lectures (oops) exams are all online + not proctored. Professor is interesting and engaging but just not my thing as I'm not an anthro major. LOVED my TA she was so so knowledgable and such a good teacher so I actually enjoyed going to discussion where attendance is mandatory. Mostly just busy work not super challenging.

I genuinely looked forward to this class every day we met. Discussions were lively and engaging. Papers were graded a bit more harshly than I think most of anthro professors I've had; however, I never felt like the grading was unfair.
